questions.question: Which psql meta-command lists the tables visible in the current search path?
questions.explanation: \dt lists tables; \l lists databases, \du roles, and \c connects.

questions.question: Which PostgreSQL column type is the classic shorthand for an auto-incrementing integer backed by a sequence?
questions.explanation: SERIAL creates an integer column with a default from an owned sequence.

questions.question: Which operator concatenates two text values in PostgreSQL?
questions.explanation: || is the SQL-standard string concatenation operator used by PostgreSQL.

questions.question: Which clause makes an INSERT return the generated id of the new row?
questions.explanation: PostgreSQL's RETURNING clause returns values from inserted, updated or deleted rows.

questions.question: Which statement creates a role named app that is allowed to log in?
questions.explanation: Roles get the LOGIN attribute via CREATE ROLE ... LOGIN (CREATE USER implies LOGIN).

questions.question: Which index type does a plain CREATE INDEX build by default?
questions.explanation: B-tree is the default access method for CREATE INDEX.

questions.question: Which type stores JSON in a decomposed binary form that supports GIN indexing?
questions.explanation: jsonb stores parsed binary JSON and supports GIN indexes; json stores the raw text.

questions.question: Which command quickly removes all rows from a table without scanning them row by row?
questions.explanation: TRUNCATE empties the table by reclaiming its storage instead of deleting rows individually; DROP removes the table itself.

questions.question: Given data jsonb, which operator returns the value of key name as text?
questions.explanation: ->> extracts a field as text, while -> returns it as jsonb.

questions.question: Which jsonb operator tests whether the left value contains the right value?
questions.explanation: @> is "contains"; <@ is "is contained by" and ? tests for a key.

questions.question: What does EXPLAIN ANALYZE do that plain EXPLAIN does not?
options: Rewrites the query into a faster form
Executes the query and reports actual times and row counts
questions.explanation: EXPLAIN shows the estimated plan; ANALYZE actually runs the statement and adds real measurements.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of VACUUM?
options: Reclaiming space used by dead row versions left by updates and deletes
Forcing WAL to be flushed to disk
questions.explanation: Under MVCC, old row versions remain until VACUUM marks their space reusable.

questions.question: Which index type is normally used to speed up jsonb containment (@>) queries?
questions.explanation: GIN indexes the keys and values inside jsonb, supporting @> and key-existence operators.

questions.question: Which statement gives role r read access to all existing tables in schema public?
options: GRANT READ ON public TO r;
ALTER SCHEMA public GRANT SELECT TO r;
GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO r;
GRANT USAGE ON ALL TABLES TO r;
questions.explanation: GRANT ... ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA grants the privilege on every existing table in that schema.

questions.question: Which PostgreSQL syntax updates the existing row when an INSERT hits a unique-key conflict?
questions.explanation: INSERT ... ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE is PostgreSQL's upsert; the others are MySQL syntax or invalid.

questions.question: What does CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY avoid compared with a normal CREATE INDEX?
options: Blocking inserts, updates and deletes on the table during the build
questions.explanation: A concurrent build does not take a lock that blocks writes, at the cost of a slower build.

questions.question: Under PostgreSQL MVCC, what happens physically when a row is updated?
options: The row is overwritten in place
A new row version is written and the old one is marked expired
The old values move to an undo log
The page stays locked until VACUUM runs
questions.explanation: PostgreSQL writes a new tuple version; the old one becomes dead once no snapshot needs it.

questions.question: In READ COMMITTED, PostgreSQL's default level, which snapshot does each statement see?
options: A snapshot taken when that statement starts
A snapshot taken when the transaction started
questions.explanation: Each statement in READ COMMITTED takes a fresh snapshot of data committed before it began.

questions.question: What is a partial index?
options: An index on only the first N characters of a column
An index created on only some partitions
An index built with a WHERE predicate so it covers only matching rows
questions.explanation: A partial index includes only rows satisfying its WHERE clause, keeping it small.

questions.question: What must be true for an Index Only Scan to skip heap fetches for most rows?
options: The index is a GIN index
The visibility map marks those pages all-visible
questions.explanation: Without the all-visible bit, PostgreSQL must visit the heap to check row visibility.

questions.question: What does freezing (anti-wraparound vacuum) protect against?
options: Old rows appearing to be in the future after transaction ID wraparound
questions.explanation: Transaction IDs are 32-bit; freezing old tuples prevents them becoming invisible when IDs wrap around.

questions.question: Which feature lets a table restrict which rows each role can see or modify?
questions.explanation: With RLS enabled, CREATE POLICY expressions filter the rows visible to each role.
